title: Minting NFTs
section: 42. Minting NFTs and Building an NFT Marketplace like OpenSea
summary: Starts the OpenD project: downloads the starter, adds a separate NFT canister file registered in dfx.json, converts it from a plain actor to an actor class taking name, owner and image bytes, adds query getters, and mints a first NFT from the command line with dfx deploy --argument.

concepts.heading: Starter project and layout
points: Download the opend starter zip from the lecture resources, unzip, move it into the projects folder and open in VS Code.

src contains an almost empty main.mo (the future marketplace backend: listing, buying) and a frontend assets folder with pre-written HTML/CSS; many long class names but each is just an element with styling.
The learning focus is making backend and frontend cooperate, not the styling.

concepts.heading: Why the NFT gets its own canister file
points: main.mo is the e-commerce backend. Each NFT, however, is a separately instantiated canister, so its code should not live in main.mo.
Create src/NFT/nft.mo.

Register it in dfx.json: add a new entry in the canisters object (placing it right after the first canister entry avoids comma mistakes) with 'main' set to src/NFT/nft.mo and 'type' set to motoko. The canister name used on the CLI is the key, e.g. nft.

concepts.heading: Smoke test with a plain actor
points: First write actor NFT { Debug.print("It works."); } with import Debug from mo:base/Debug.
Run npm install (installs the many dependencies in package.json, takes a few minutes), then dfx start in one terminal and dfx deploy in another.
The dfx start terminal should print the message from the nft canister. If not: restart dfx start, check dfx.json syntax, file names and the path.

concepts.heading: Actor class = a canister factory
points: Add the class keyword: actor class NFT(...) and give it constructor parameters. A plain actor takes no input; an actor class takes arguments when created, which lets code create canisters programmatically from user input (needed for minting later).
Parameters: name : Text, owner : Principal (requires import Principal from mo:base/Principal), content : [Nat8] (the image as an array of 8-bit natural numbers, i.e. raw bytes).
Inside the class, copy the parameters into fields: itemName = name, nftOwner = owner, imageBytes = content.
Every canister instance gets a unique principal id when created, which is what makes each NFT unique and non-interchangeable.
(Extra) Newer Motoko versions want the persistent keyword before actor class; the reference repo uses persistent actor class.

concepts.heading: Query getters
points: public query func getName() : async Text returns itemName.
getOwner() : async Principal returns nftOwner.
getAsset() : async [Nat8] returns imageBytes.
query functions read state quickly without going through consensus; fine for read-only access.

concepts.heading: Deploying an actor class needs arguments
points: Plain dfx deploy nft now fails with 'Invalid data: Expected arguments, but found none', because the init arguments are required.

Pass them with --argument followed by a single-quoted Candid tuple: three values separated by commas, a text in double quotes, the owner as principal "...", and the bytes as vec { ... } of numbers. The README in the lesson supplies the full command with the byte data of a 10x10 pixel hat image.
Get your own principal with dfx identity get-principal and replace the one in the command, keeping the formatting exactly (quotes after the word principal).
Run the whole deploy command; it deploys all canisters and hands the argument to the nft one.
NFT name in the demo: a CryptoDunks title with a number, mimicking OpenSea-style naming.

concepts.heading: Verifying
points: dfx canister call nft getName returns the name; getOwner returns the principal; getAsset returns a long list of numbers.
No parentheses are written after the function name on the CLI.
The bytes are raw image data and not readable; viewing it requires the frontend, built in the next lesson.

code_examples.caption: src/NFT/nft.mo (final)
Mint from the CLI and verify
code_examples.code:
dfx identity get-principal
dfx deploy nft --argument '("CryptoDunks #123", principal "<YOUR_PRINCIPAL>", vec {10; 20; 30})'   # real command carries the full byte list from the README
dfx canister call nft getName
dfx canister call nft getOwner
dfx canister call nft getAsset

task.name: Create and mint the NFT canister
task.starting_point: Unzipped opend starter with empty main.mo and prebuilt frontend.
task.goal: A deployed nft canister, created with an actor class, that returns the name, owner and image bytes you gave it.
steps: Create src/NFT/nft.mo and add the nft entry to dfx.json.
Write a plain actor that prints a message; run npm install, dfx start, dfx deploy and confirm the message.
Change it to actor class NFT(name, owner, content) and copy parameters into itemName, nftOwner, imageBytes.
Add query functions getName, getOwner, getAsset.
Get your principal with dfx identity get-principal.
Deploy with --argument using the README command, substituting your principal.
Call getName, getOwner and getAsset with dfx canister call and compare with what you passed.
task.expected_result: getName returns the minted name, getOwner returns your principal, getAsset returns the byte vector.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 42 - Minting NFTs and Building an NFT Marketplace like OpenSea/42.02 Minting NFTs/OPEND/src/NFT/nft.mo

pitfalls: Wrong path or JSON comma in dfx.json: canister not found or not deployed.
Deploying an actor class without --argument gives the 'Expected arguments' error.
Altering the spacing or quotes in the argument string.
Not replacing the sample principal with your own.
Typos in query function names; CLI call uses getName without ().
(Extra) The reference main.mo is still the default greet stub in this lesson, so it only matters for the nft canister.

playground.coverage: No playground lesson yet (section 42 has no playground file).
gaps_and_ideas: Proposed lesson 'Actor classes as canister factories': blurb comparing a singleton actor with a class that produces many instances, each with a unique id.

Tasks: 1) turn an actor into an actor class with three parameters; 2) add getters; 3) write the deploy --argument string for given values; 4) call the getters; 5) explain why two NFTs with identical data still differ.
Starter code: JavaScript class NFT with constructor(name, owner, bytes) and an id generator.
Explore demo idea: a 'mint' form that constructs instances with fresh random ids and lists them, plus a CLI-argument builder that prints the correctly formatted Candid string.
